title: Trace playback through edge and control-plane failure
description: Choose an incident, then compare mitigations. The model shows a simplified playback route and user impact; real systems need regional, ISP, title, device, and package-version evidence before broad steering.

nodes.label: Netflix client
nodes.responsibility: Holds a playback buffer, downloads segments, applies ABR, and reports session quality.

nodes.label: Playback control
nodes.responsibility: Validates entitlement and package availability, then returns a manifest and delivery guidance.

nodes.label: Preferred edge
nodes.responsibility: Serves cached segments from the nearby delivery location.

nodes.label: Alternate edge
nodes.responsibility: Receives steered traffic when the preferred edge or its route is unsafe.

nodes.label: Package origin
nodes.responsibility: Supplies validated segments for controlled cache fills and holds the complete package.

nodes.label: Access network
nodes.responsibility: Carries segment bytes between the chosen edge and the viewer device.

mitigations.label: Hold current route and retry
mitigations.detail: Keep the existing destination and allow bounded client retry.

mitigations.label: Coalesce fills and lower safely
mitigations.detail: Deduplicate cache fills, bound origin work, and use a lower sustainable rendition.

mitigations.label: Steer to a healthy fallback
mitigations.detail: Move new or failing work to an alternate edge or stable control response.

scenarios.label: Cache miss storm
scenarios.detail: A newly popular package is absent from the local cache, so many players request the same early segments.

hold-and-retry.blastRadius: Popular title in one edge region
hold-and-retry.result: Independent retries multiply identical origin fills and make both startup and origin protection worse.
recovery: Detect the hit-rate cliff and repeated object keys.
Rate-limit unsafe retries at the edge and player policy boundary.
Warm the package only after origin queues return to a bounded level.

coalesce-and-degrade.result: One fill serves waiting requests while ABR prefers a lower ready rendition, protecting origin concurrency.
recovery: Coalesce requests by package version and segment key.
Cap fill concurrency and serve ready lower renditions where possible.
Verify hit rate, fill wait, and origin queue depth before releasing limits.

steer-and-fallback.result: Steering can spread load, but an alternate edge without the package may simply move the miss storm unless its cache state is known.
recovery: Confirm alternate-edge cache availability before broad steering.
Move a bounded cohort and observe origin miss amplification.
Keep coalescing enabled until both caches are warm.

scenarios.label: Preferred edge outage
scenarios.detail: The nearest edge cannot serve segments because its process, appliance, or upstream route is unavailable.

hold-and-retry.blastRadius: All viewers pinned to the failed edge
hold-and-retry.result: Retrying a dead destination consumes the playback buffer without creating a route to media.
recovery: Quarantine the failed edge from new assignments.
Expire or override stale delivery guidance.
Confirm players can receive a replacement route.

coalesce-and-degrade.blastRadius: All viewers pinned to the failed edge
coalesce-and-degrade.result: Lowering rendition cannot help when no segment path is reachable; it only becomes useful after route recovery.
recovery: Remove the failed edge from steering first.
Preserve buffered playback where possible.
Apply a conservative rendition only on the replacement path.

steer-and-fallback.result: A healthy alternate edge restores media delivery, though a longer route may require an immediate ABR step-down.
recovery: Fence the failed edge from assignment.
Issue alternate delivery guidance and retry the current segment once.
Watch startup, rebuffering, and alternate-edge reserve before returning traffic.

scenarios.label: Package origin degradation
scenarios.detail: The origin is slow or erroring, so cache fills become unreliable even though some edge hits still work.

hold-and-retry.result: Retries add work to an already slow origin and may convert a partial fill problem into a broader outage.
recovery: Stop retry amplification and identify the failing origin dependency.
Protect existing edge hits from eviction pressure.
Recover origin capacity before reopening uncontrolled fills.

coalesce-and-degrade.result: The edge preserves cached segments and lower ready renditions while a small number of fills wait behind bounded origin work.
recovery: Prioritize cache-resident renditions and segment continuity.
Coalesce and queue only essential origin fills.
Restore higher-quality fills after origin latency and errors stabilize.

steer-and-fallback.result: A second edge helps only when it already has the needed package; otherwise origin degradation follows the request.
recovery: Check alternate cache residency before steering.
Move only the cohorts that gain a cache hit.
Keep origin admission bounded across both edges.

scenarios.label: Manifest failure
scenarios.detail: Playback control cannot issue or validate a manifest for a new session, even though media may still be cached.

hold-and-retry.result: The edge cannot authorize or describe a new playback package; retrying the failed control endpoint delays startup.
recovery: Separate new-session failures from active-session continuity.
Rate-limit retries and inspect entitlement, signing, and package-version signals.
Restore a valid control response before advertising normal startup.

coalesce-and-degrade.result: A lower rendition is not selectable without a valid manifest, so media-side mitigation does not repair the control failure.
recovery: Keep active sessions on their existing manifest where policy permits.
Fail new starts honestly rather than exposing stale authorization.
Repair the control dependency and validate a signed manifest end to end.

steer-and-fallback.result: A healthy control-plane fallback can issue a valid manifest, after which normal cached media delivery resumes.
recovery: Fence the failed manifest issuer or configuration version.
Route a bounded cohort to a compatible healthy control endpoint.
Verify authorization, package version, startup time, and edge delivery together.

scenarios.label: Viewer network loss
scenarios.detail: The access network loses throughput or packets while the control plane and edges remain healthy.

hold-and-retry.blastRadius: One access network or viewer cohort
hold-and-retry.result: Repeatedly asking for the same high rendition does not create bandwidth; the player drains its buffer and pauses.
recovery: Detect sustained download loss rather than one slow segment.
Avoid uncontrolled parallel retries on the same access path.
Resume from the current segment when usable throughput returns.

coalesce-and-degrade.blastRadius: One access network or viewer cohort
coalesce-and-degrade.result: ABR chooses a lower sustainable rendition and preserves buffer when some capacity remains; it does not hide a complete disconnection.
recovery: Step down on buffer and throughput evidence.
Retry a bounded number of segment requests after backoff.
Upgrade only after several stable transfers refill the buffer.

steer-and-fallback.blastRadius: One access network or viewer cohort
steer-and-fallback.result: Changing edges may help if the route is the problem, but it cannot repair the viewer's last-mile loss without evidence of a better path.
recovery: Compare route and transfer evidence before steering.
Move one bounded cohort to the alternate edge.
Keep ABR conservative until buffer health is restored.
